certification: Certified when every skill scores 3 or higher.

rubrics.name: Draft rubric
rubrics.short: One question per skill, levels named Poor to Excellent.
rules: For each skill, quote the learner's words that support your score and give a one-sentence reason.

empathy.question: Did the learner show empathy and understanding toward the customer?

listening.question: Did the learner listen actively to the customer?

ownership.question: Did the learner take ownership of the customer's issue?

resolution.question: Did the learner resolve the issue effectively?

close.question: Did the learner close the call professionally?

rubrics.name: Anchored rubric
rubrics.short: Each level says what it sounds like, plus five scoring rules.
rules: Score only what the learner (the agent) says. The customer's lines are context.
A level counts only if the transcript shows it. Each level includes everything in the levels below it.
If any Not yet behaviour appears, the skill is 1, whatever else the learner did.
If you are torn between two levels, choose the lower one.
Quote the learner's words exactly as written. Do not paraphrase inside a quote. If you cannot quote it, do not give credit for it.

empathy.question: Does the learner acknowledge what happened to this customer?
anchors: No acknowledgement of what happened to the customer, or words that brush it off.
Only a stock line that would fit any call, such as a general apology or a general "I understand". Nothing about this customer's situation.
Names what happened to this customer, or how it affects them, in words that fit only this call.
Proficient, and later in the call refers back to the customer's situation in words, for example when shaping the fix or at the end.

listening.question: Does the learner show they understood the problem before fixing it?
anchors: Makes the customer repeat something they already said, or answers a different question.
Asks for details the fix needs, but never plays the problem back to the customer.
Plays the problem back in their own words and checks it is right before fixing it.
Proficient, and picks up a second concern the customer mentioned in passing and deals with it.

ownership.question: Does the learner take the problem on themselves?
anchors: Blames another team, the customer or the bank, or sends the customer somewhere else instead of acting.
Action happens, but only in passive or hedged words with no "I" doing it.
Says in the first person what they are doing or have done to fix it, within the call.
Proficient, and without being asked does something extra that stops the problem coming back or saves the customer a future step.

resolution.question: Does the learner fix the problem and say what happens next?
anchors: No fix, or wrong information.
A fix, but no clear what or when: no date, time frame or amount.
The right fix, and says what will happen and by when.
Proficient, and checks the fix works for the customer's situation, or offers a choice that fits it.

close.question: Does the learner close the call so the customer knows where things stand?
anchors: Ends without a recap and without checking whether the customer needs anything else.
Checks whether the customer needs anything else, but gives no recap of what was done.
Recaps what was done and what happens next, and checks whether anything else is needed.
Proficient, and gives a reference number or a named way back if the fix does not happen.

rubrics.name: Revised rubric
rubrics.short: The anchored rubric after one round of review: one rule added, one anchor reworded.

A level counts only if the transcript shows it. Each level includes everything in the levels below it.

If you are torn between two levels, choose the lower one.
